content_html:
Multiverse Theories

“Many universes” comprises distinct ideas emerging from inflationary cosmology, quantum foundations, and string theory, each multiplying different things (regions, branches, vacua, or mathematics itself). The sharpest scientific concerns are testability (especially Levels II–IV), the eternal‑inflation measure problem, and whether anthropic reasoning explains “fine‑tuning” without veering into unfalsifiable metaphysics.

Theory Origin / Mechanism What counts as a “universe”? Potential observables Common critiques Status (2025)
Level I (cosmic-horizon plurality)
Inflation		 Standard inflation + ΛCDM; near-flat large-scale geometry implies regions beyond our horizon. Other Hubble volumes with the same laws but different initial conditions. Indirect only: flatness/structure consistent with very large spatial extent; no access beyond horizon. “Not separate universes, just far-away regions”; practically unfalsifiable. Conservative implication of inflation; conceptually uncontroversial.
See Tegmark 2003/2009.
Level II (eternal inflation bubbles)
Inflation		 Inflation ends locally, producing pocket/bubble domains with different symmetry breaking. Bubble domains with possibly different constants, low-energy physics, even dimensions. CMB “bubble collision” imprints; statistical predictions (none confirmed). Measure problem (probabilities over infinities), limited testability. Active theoretical work; empirical status unsettled.
Guth 2007; Feeney et al. 2011; Aguirre et al. 2009.
Level III (Everett / Many‑Worlds)
Quantum		 Unitary QM + decoherence; no collapse → branching of the universal wavefunction. Branches corresponding to different outcomes of quantum events. Same lab predictions as unitary QM; no agreed new empirical handle beyond interpretation. Ontological extravagance; interpretation vs. new physics; empirical indistinguishability. Major interpretation in foundations; philosophically contested.
SEP (Vaidman 2021; Barrett entry).
String Landscape
String theory		 Vast discretuum of vacua from compactifications/fluxes; often populated by eternal inflation. Each vacuum → different low‑energy physics. At best statistical/anthropic predictions; no decisive unique tests so far. Landscape size/measure ambiguities; questions of testability. Active research and criticism; no experimental confirmation.
Douglas 2019 review.
Level IV (mathematical multiverse)
Philosophy		 All consistent mathematical structures have physical existence. Different mathematics → different fundamental laws. No clear empirical leverage; primarily meta‑explanatory. Often classed as metaphysics; unfalsifiable. Philosophical proposal; not mainstream physics.
Tegmark 2003; 2009.
Anthropic selection
Cross‑cutting		 Observers arise only where parameters permit life; selection effect across many domains. Any domain (Level II/landscape etc.) that supports observers. Explains fine‑tuning qualitatively; limited predictive bite. Risk of post‑hoc reasoning; depends on prior multiverse. Used cautiously in cosmology/philosophy of science.
SEP: Fine‑Tuning.

Glossary

Measure problem: Difficulty assigning probabilities when eternal inflation yields infinitely many regions/outcomes.

Bubble collision: Hypothesized imprint in the CMB when inflationary bubbles interact; searches to date are inconclusive.

Decoherence: Environment‑induced suppression of interference, making quantum branches effectively classical.

Landscape: The set of metastable string vacua yielding different low‑energy physics.
